question: Which permanent `tools.fs` contract should OpenClaw adopt, and should its security guarantee include arbitrary shell-mediated filesystem access?
rationale: Two open implementations propose different public schemas and enforcement semantics, while both leave an important exec-boundary choice unresolved; automation cannot safely select that product and security contract.

options.title: Typed roots with explicit exec limits
options.body: Adopt read-only/read-write file and directory roots for file and media tools, while documenting and separately solving arbitrary exec isolation.

options.title: Deny-wins path rules
options.body: Adopt `allowedPaths` and `denyPaths` with equivalent canonicalization, access-mode, TOCTOU, compatibility, and documentation guarantees.

options.title: Require a unified sandbox boundary
options.body: Pause both file-tool-focused candidates until shell-mediated filesystem access can be isolated or enforced under the same policy.

recommendation.title: Typed roots with explicit exec limits
recommendation.body: Adopt read-only/read-write file and directory roots for file and media tools, while documenting and separately solving arbitrary exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has already reviewed this exact gap and framed the unresolved configuration and exec-security boundary for maintainer follow-up.
